title: What If the Netherlands Stopped Defending Against the Sea?

scenes.text: What if the Netherlands stopped defending itself from the sea? A quarter of the country sits below it.
About 26 percent of the land lies below sea level, and that includes the country's main airport.
Roughly 60 percent of the territory could flood. More than half of its 17 million people live in those low areas.
Those areas produce over 70 percent of the national income, and 17,500 kilometers of dikes, dunes, and barriers guard them.
It has happened before. In 1953 a North Sea storm flooded the southwest, killing 1,835 people and leaving 72,000 homeless.
So the Dutch built storm barriers, one nine kilometers long with 64 steel doors. The sea never stops, and neither can they.
